defs.def: not going or allowing you to go at a fast speed 慢速的；低速的

ex.s: It's important to slow down and think about food as something nutritious rather than just something to eat in between meetings. ____17____ It actually takes a few minutes for your brain to tell your body that it has had enough food, so eat slowly and stop eating before you feel full.
ex.t: 重要的是要放慢脚步，将食物视为有营养的东西，而不仅仅是在会议之间吃的东西。____ 17 ____实际上，你的大脑需要几分钟的时间来告诉你的身体已经有足够的食物，所以要慢慢吃，在感到饱之前停止进食。

ex.s: 38    So, slow down and think what you really want to do at that moment.
ex.t: 38所以，慢下来，想想那一刻你真正想做的事情。

ex.s: According to an evolutionary psychology theory that a person's “life strategy” slows down or speeds up depending on his or her ___47___, exposure to a “harsh and unpredictable” environment leads to faster development, while a more resource-rich and secure environment has the ___48___ effect, the study said.
ex.t: 根据一种进化心理学理论,一个人的“生活策略”视他或她的 47   而放慢或加速,接触“危险和不可预测的”环境会导致更快的发展,而资源更丰富和更安全的环境则具有 48   的效果。

ex.s: Slowly but surely, my efforts to adjust to the new routine paid off.
ex.t: 慢慢但肯定地，我适应新日常生活的努力得到了回报。

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 人人都是这样学会阅读的。我们从句子开始,然后是段落,然后是故事。这似乎是一个无止境的旅程,但作为一个六岁女孩,我意识到如何阅读可以打开许多门。当妈妈说“C-A-N-D-Y藏在顶层的架子上”时,我知道糖果在哪里。我阅读的进展提高了我的好奇心,我想知道一切。我常常发现自己告诉我妈开车要慢一点,这样我就能读出我们通过的所有路标。

ex.s: So, my dad and I put on our new cowboy hats, got on our horses, and headed slowly towards the mountains.
ex.t: 于是，我和爸爸戴上新的牛仔帽，骑上马，慢慢地向山区走去。

ex.s: When we slow down, we create space to reflect on our thoughts and emotions, which helps us identify important areas of our lives and ___13___ (give) us the opportunity to make right choices.

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．
ex.t: 最近,我构思了一个与地球环境相关的新计时方法, 条件可能因全球变暖而改变。我们现在正在安克雷奇博物馆建造一个钟表, 反映几条阿拉斯加主要河流的总流量, 这些河流对当地和全球环境变化很敏感。我们已经计划它与原子钟相匹配, 如果水道以目前的速度继续流动。 如果河流在未来平均运行得更快, 时钟会比标准时间提前。如果它们运行得慢, 你会看到相反的效果。

ex.s: “But we all have to accept that as we get older our reactions slow down and this often results in people avoiding any potentially challenging driving conditions and losing confidence in their driving skills.
ex.t: “但我们都必须接受，随着年龄的增长，我们的反应会减慢，这通常会导致人们避免任何可能具有挑战性的驾驶条件，并对自己的驾驶技能失去信心。

ex.s: By painting buildings white, cities may slow down the warming process.
